title: Machine formats carry the same stitches, trims and colour stops as PE-DESIGN 11's exports
description: One small design with every machine-level event: a trim inside a colour (two Red running lines 40 mm apart), a colour change (Black after Red), and 15 mm satin stitches that the relative formats have to split. PE-DESIGN 11 opens OpenStitch's a.pes as stitches and exports it to each format; the exports are compared record by record with OpenStitch's own writers: how a frame move, a trim, a colour change and a long stitch are written, the header fields and the origin. The writers follow PE-DESIGN's layout (crates/openstitch-formats/src/layout.rs; docs/FILE_FORMATS.md).

featureMatrix.feature: JEF read/write (Janome chart, stops, hoop code)
PCS read/write (1/6 mm grid, hoop byte)
HUS read and write (LZ77 + Huffman streams, HUS chart)
VIP read and write (HUS streams, obfuscated RGB colour table)

evidence.note: PE-DESIGN 11.50 PES files (177 files, compat/reference and the owner's round-2 folders, 2026-10-27): every interior frame move carries the PEC trim flag; plain jumps appear only as the first record and right after a colour change; no zero-length stitch record
DST: 3-byte records, jump flag, colour change 0xC3; a trim is a run of jumps (count is a machine setting)

PE-DESIGN 11.50's exports of this design in DST, EXP, PCS, HUS, VIP, JEF, SEW and XXX (compat/reference/machine, 2026-10-27): a stitch longer than a record is a jump plus a stitch (HUS: two stitches); a frame move is a jump run with no trim record (DST pads it to three jump records with zero-length jumps; XXX writes a trimmed move as one 7E record; VIP writes 88; HUS a zero-length jump); JEF, SEW, XXX and VIP fold the move's remainder into the first stitch after it; DST, EXP and XXX jump back to the origin at the end; PCS writes a fixed 16-colour table and indexes it from the colour-change records

SEW start point (pe-refs-3, 2026-10-28, compat/reference/machine/sew-a-moved10.* and sew-square-centre.*): PE-DESIGN's SEW export of machine-formats' design moved 10 mm right and down is byte-identical to the one in place, so the stream is relative to the design; its first record moves from a start point 15.9 mm left of and 9.7 mm above the design centre to the first needle point as one stitch (a jump and a stitch for the square's 24.9 mm way; the same offset from the square's centre). OpenStitch's SEW writer starts at (-15.9, -9.7) mm from the centre; the SEW reader keeps that first move. The square's export also shows PE-DESIGN exporting its own objects from their first needle point, the end of the PEC's first jump (the tie-in: there, 0.3 mm back, there again), which the PES reader does not take as a needle point: one record more in PE-DESIGN's stream, the rest identical.

references.make: Run `stitchtool compat --only machine-formats` and open target/compat/work/machine-formats/a.pes in PE-DESIGN 11 (two Red running lines (20,20)-(60,20) and (20,60)-(60,60) mm with a trim between them, then a Black satin rectangle (20,30)-(60,45) mm with 15 mm stitches across it). Change nothing. File > Export (or Save As with the other-format type list) as Tajima DST under the file name given; record every option PE-DESIGN offers for the export (for DST: the number of jumps for a trim) and its value, the PE-DESIGN version, the date and the operating system in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json.

machine.make: Sew target/compat/work/machine-formats/a.pes on a Brother single-needle machine (medium-weight woven cotton, tear-away stabiliser): the two Red lines must sew with one thread cut between them (no thread span across the 40 mm gap), the machine must stop once for Black, and the satin must sew its 15 mm stitches whole with no needle holes along the long edges. Record the result, the cut, and whether the machine showed the design as 40 x 40 mm.

measurements.evidence: the 40 mm move between the two Red lines is the only trim; the colour change carries its own cut
PE-DESIGN 11 keeps satin stitches whole in PES up to 15 mm (stitch-sweeps S8, sweep-satin-width-15.pes); the machine formats split them at their own limits
PE-DESIGN 11's DST export of the same stitches: the same needle points, jumps for the trim and colour stop, and the same split of the 15 mm stitches
PE-DESIGN 11's EXP export of the same stitches
PE-DESIGN 11's JEF export of the same stitches
PE-DESIGN 11's PCS export of the same stitches (PCS units are 1/6 mm, so 0.2 mm of rounding)

PE-DESIGN 11's SEW export of the same stitches. PE-DESIGN starts the stream 15.9 mm left of and 9.7 mm above the design centre and sews the way to the first needle point as a stitch; the stream is design-relative (sew-a-moved10.sew, the same design moved 10 mm on the page, is byte-identical; sew-square-centre.sew, a 20 x 20 mm square, starts at the same offset from its centre). OpenStitch starts there too, so the records are identical from the first one.
